note: Video 007 'The Lesson': Black & Gold Noir. Every shot matches its caption; 'set' is the engine set, 'world' the area inside it. Transitions: sand (a wall of blowing sand sweeps across), rain (a dissolve through rain on glass), black (a fade through black with grain); every other cut is a hard cut.

shots.why: I always say, one of the greatest lessons: a slow push through the rainy window into the dark room
I took in and absorbed during my illness: he lies still, the monitor line glowing
I came to see the dunya as worthless: an endless dark desert, the wind lifting sand off a crest
a nice car: a ghost-gold car on the dunes crumbles to sand from front to back
a house, these worldly things: a ghost-gold house rises out of the sand, lights on, then pours away like an hourglass
they didn't mean much in my heart: his hand on his chest, a slow orbit, one small real-gold glow
when I'm in hospital: the IV drip falling in slow motion, the monitor beeping
at my worst: a long corridor, flickering lights
the hardest stages of my health: heavier rain on the glass, the room behind it
even if you had palaces, what would that palace do for you?: the camera rises up a towering ghost-gold palace, which collapses into a sandstorm
you're ill, on your deathbed: top-down over the bed, a slow pull up, the room small and dark
servants and attendants, cars and palaces: a row of faceless ghost servants, cars and palaces glowing cold gold
what's the use?: one by one they crumble to sand
what would they do for you?: top-down over the dunes, the wind carrying it all away (no person)
the dunya has no value: a huge empty dune at night, one tiny figure
it comes from lowliness: the camera sinks low, sand trickling down into a low hollow
took to heart on my deathbed: his fingers tightening on the sheet; lightning at the window
...on my deathbed: the monitor line, the room
the dunya has no value: the gold light in his chest grows
strong faith: warm light spreads across the bed and the room; the rain on the window catches gold
I began to want the Hereafter: dawn, he walks out of the hospital doors into the first light
to strive for it and prepare for it: he walks across the dunes toward the sunrise, his footprints in gold
the Hereafter is the foundation: a stone foundation glowing in the sand; the sand blows over everything else but not over it
it has taken most of my heart: he stands on the crest facing the rising sun, a slow crane up into the gold
